T01.answer:
A score of 66 receives a **B-** in the Terminal.

Per the engine logic, grades are assigned in Postgres inside the scoring function, not the front end: score ≥ 90 is A+, ≥ 85 A, ≥ 80 A-, ≥ 75 B+, ≥ 70 B, ≥ 65 B-, ≥ 60 C+, ≥ 52 C, ≥ 40 D, else F [S4]. Since 66 falls at or above 65 but below 70, it lands on B-.

Two caveats worth knowing: the engine grades the *unrounded* score while the stored `risk_adjusted_score` is rounded to 0.1, so a property sitting within 0.05 of the 65 boundary could display one grade off from its stored value [S1]. Also, the grades you see are derived at display time rather than persisted — `v43.recompute_batch` writes only score, IRR, and sigma [S1]. The bands themselves are reconstructed in the documentation by matching published grade counts to score percentiles, so they reproduce published output within data-quality drift rather than being read from the operational mapping [S2]. The authoritative check for any specific property is its `risk_adjusted_score` in the Spain Terminal.

T03.answer:
No — in the Terminal a "scored" property only means the model ran, not that the inputs behind the score were real or complete [S1].

Measured live on October 21, 2026 over the scorable multifamily universe (clean `dq_status`, 5+ units) — 587,802 properties at that time — every record had a v43 score, expected IRR and run lineage, even where inputs were absent [S1]. The Terminal's own documentation flags this as the core coverage weakness and proposes fixes: compute uncertainty (sigma) per record from the inputs actually present so fully defaulted records show wide bands, and display input completeness plus which inputs were defaulted on every score [S4].

Practically, treat a score as a model output whose reliability varies by record. Check the property's input completeness and defaulted-input flags alongside the score in Spain Terminal; the actual values must be read there. Note the snapshot figures are dated — the universe has since grown to 634,930 after the FL NAL ingest, and after the v50.0 rescore (October 23, 2026, 06:28 UTC) the mean score is 41.90 with mean expected IRR 11.55%, but that doesn't change the "ran ≠ real inputs" distinction [S1][S2].
